elements.element: No obligation on Customer to deal exclusively with Vendor / use Vendor as sole supplier
elements.evidence: 7.2 as revised imposes no exclusive-dealing duty; clause now reads Customer "is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer"; no other sole-supplier language remains

elements.element: No de facto exclusivity mechanic (right of first refusal / disclose-and-match condition) restricting Customer's engagement of other providers
elements.evidence: the operative duty "must disclose and match for Vendor" is replaced with "is not required to disclose or match for Vendor", so engaging another provider is unconditioned

elements.element: Exclusivity confined to a defined product category
elements.evidence: clause contains no exclusivity grant or product-category scope at all after the flip

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: no service-level or delivery-date termination trigger appears in the revised 7.2

reasons: The single replacement flips the disclose-and-match operator, eliminating the right-of-first-refusal mechanic that operated as de facto exclusivity on Customer; the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation) is therefore fully met.

Fallback elements (defined category, 12-month cap, automatic end on SLA/delivery failure) are absent, but that is immaterial because the drafter's locked target is preferred and the preferred bargain is satisfied without borrowing from the fallback.
Change is confined to one operator phrase within the same sentence; no new exception, boilerplate, or whole-clause rewrite, so minimality holds.

No undefined terms or contradictions introduced; the revised clause is consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that no exclusivity or MFC commitment was given, and all other commercial terms are untouched.
